USB audio allows you to listen to your audio source through a USB-C wired connection, offering a digital and “lossless” audio quality; hear exactly what was created without any loss of the original data. This is particularly useful for USB-C source devices such as computers or mobile devices when gaming or listening to lossless audio files. Over a USB-C connection using USB audio, the QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) can receive audio signals at 16-bit, 44.1kHz or 48kHz from compatible source files.

##

In Aware Mode, when ActiveSense is enabled, your headphones will automatically activate and adjust noise cancellation in response to your environment’s noise level in order to keep your surrounding noise levels more constant. This way, you can remain aware of your surroundings without having your music drowned out by interruptions like loud appliance motor noises such as a coffee grinder or blender. ActiveSense can be enabled and disabled in the Aware Mode setting.

##

QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) have three control inputs on the right earcup: a Bluetooth/power button at the bottom, a multi-function button in the back, and a capacitive volume/shortcut-activation strip along the back edge. Additionally, the headphones are equipped with on-head/off-head detection, which is another way to control the product.

• The Bluetooth/power button is used to power the headphones on/off, put the headphones in pairing mode, cycle through paired devices, and more.

• The multi-function button supports audio playback (e.g., play/pause/skip), telephone calls (e.g., answer/decline calls), mode switching (e.g., Quiet, Aware, Immersion), and more.

• Swiping along the volume strip changes volume, and pressing and holding it activates a user-configurable shortcut.

• Putting the headphones on and taking them off controls wake/sleep/auto-off and resume/pause. Auto-off can be customized in the Bose app.

##

QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) will automatically disconnect after 10 min and then transition to low power (sleep) when they are off your head for a total of 30 minutes. If you prefer to quickly disconnect the headphones within a few seconds, lay them flat on a horizontal surface (earcups facing up or down). To resume using your headphones even days/weeks later, simply put them back on your head and wait a few seconds for them to power on (listen for tones and voice prompts).

The headphones can also be manually powered on and off using the Bluetooth/power button at the bottom of the right earcup. To turn off, press and hold the Bluetooth/power button until you hear a strum tone, then release the button. To turn back on, press the Bluetooth/power button and put the headphones back on your head; wait a few seconds for tones and voice prompts (if enabled) to indicate the headphones are ready for playback.

##

Favorites allow you to choose which listening modes are accessible using the multi-function button on the right earcup. Press and hold the button, and each of your favorite modes is announced in sequence. When you hear the mode you want, release the button.

You can change your favorites in the Bose app. You can save up to 10 favorite listening modes to cycle through from your headphones, but many more listening modes can be set and managed from the Bose app.

##

A shortcut enables you to quickly and easily access a function of your choice by touching and holding the volume strip on the right earcup of your QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen). By default, the shortcut is turned off. You can turn it on and choose to have the shortcut cycle through Immersive Audio settings (Still, Motion, and Off), activate Spotify Tap, use your mobile device’s voice assistant, or read out the remaining battery life.

When you press and hold the volume strip, your voice assistant will listen for a command from the microphones in your headphones.

## Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) - Product Page Summary

The Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) is a premium over-ear wireless headphone product currently priced at **$399.00** (originally $449.00, save $50 through August 23, 2026). The product page is from Bose's official website and details the next-generation of their flagship noise-cancelling headphones.

**Key Features:**
- **CustomTune technology** – adapts sound to the unique shape of the user's ears for personalized audio
- **Bose's best noise cancellation** – with next-gen ActiveSense technology that smooths noise spikes
- **Bose Immersive Audio** – spatialized audio for music and movies, with a new Cinema Mode for enhanced video content
- **Plush comfort** – refined design with polished metal, protein leather ear cushions, and even pressure distribution
- **Battery life**: Up to 30 hours (23 hours with Immersive Audio enabled); 15-minute quick charge = 3 hours of playback
- **Bluetooth 5.4** with 30ft range; supports USB-C wired lossless audio (16-bit, 44.1kHz or 48kHz)
- **Bose App** compatibility for EQ customization, mode management, and firmware updates
- **Listening modes**: Quiet (full ANC), Aware (lets outside in), Immersion (spatialized audio), and Cinema Mode

**Specifications:**

- Materials: Plastic, aluminum, protein leather
- Rechargeable battery (3-hour charge time), USB-C interface

**What's in the box:** Headphones, carry case, 3.5mm to 2.5mm audio cable, USB-C cable (39"), safety sheet. Power adapter not included.

**BoseCare Protection Plans:** Extended warranty options available including 3-year accidental protection (covers drops, spills, mechanical breakdown, battery failure) and a 3-year standard plan.

**Buying Benefits:** 30-day return policy, price match promise, free shipping on orders $49+, Klarna/Afterpay buy-now-pay-later options.

**Comparison with Bose QuietComfort Headphones ($359):** The Ultra 2nd Gen offers Immersive Audio, ActiveSense, CustomTune, premium design materials, longer battery life (30h vs 24h), and faster quick charge (15min=3h vs 2.5h).

# Bose just dropped new QuietComfort headphones: Great ANC at a mid-range price

## Table of Contents

Few names in headphones are as iconic as the Bose QuietComfort line, and as of Aug. 6, a new addition to it is here.

The [Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen) headphones](https://zdcs.link/aN5DGD?pageview_type=Standard&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Bose%20QuietComfort%20%282nd%20gen%29%20headphones&object_type=article&object_uuid=06TEU4o8kkYW797TwPquPLx&short_url=aN5DGD&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Farticle-route-prefix%2Ftech%2Fbose-quietcomfort-headphones-2nd-gen-release-price "(opens in a new window)") come with a new design, upgraded noise cancellation, and audio features, all for the same price as the first generation headphones — $359. The headphones are available to preorder as of Aug. 8 on Bose's website and will be widely available on Aug. 13.

My testing unit of the new headphones is on the way, but ahead of preorders opening, I've gathered everything you need to know about Bose's latest headphones launch.

## Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen) at a glance

![mint and mauve headphones](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06TEU4o8kkYW797TwPquPLx/images-2.fill.size_2000x2000.v1785962841.jpg)

In addition to the classic black and white headphones, the second-gen Bose QuietComforts will come in a two-toned mint, mauve, and green colorway.  Credit: Bose

### Specs

* **Active noise cancellation:** Yes, with manual adjustment available
* **Microphones:** Six
* **Lossless playback:** Wired USB-C audio up to 24bit/48kHz
* **Equalizer:** Three-band custom equalizer
* **Spatial audio:** Bose TrueSpatial technology with Immersive Audio modes for Still, Motion, and Cinema
* **Battery life:** 24 hours per charge (18 hours with Immersive Audio)
* **Quick charge:** 15-minute charge for 2.5 hours of playback
* **Connection:** Bluetooth 5.4
* **Multipoint:** Yes
* **Weight:** 0.5 pounds
* **Colors:** Black, white smoke, eucalyptus green\*, dewdrop mint\*, rosewood mauve\* (\*limited edition colors)

### Price

The second generation Bose QuietComfort headphones will retail for $359, putting them at the same price point as the first gen QuietComforts. If you're looking for an even more affordable option, the older headphones are often on sale for under $300.

This also puts them at a considerably cheaper price point than the [Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd gen)](https://mashable.com/review/bose-quietcomfort-ultra-headphones-2nd-gen), which cost $449, and have been our pick over the standard QuietComfort headphones due to their slightly better comfort, presence of spatial audio, and slightly better ANC. With improvements on all three coming on the second gen QC headphones, it will be interesting to see how wide the gap remains between the two options.

## What's new with the Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen) headphones?

The Mashable team loves the Bose QuietComfort headphones. Lead Shopping Reporter [Samantha Mangino calls them her](https://mashable.com/article/bose-quietcomfort-headphones-review) "go-to headphones for everything," praising their solid ANC, rich sound quality, and incredibly comfortable design that's glasses and earrings-friendly. She also appreciates the tactile on-ear controls that are intuitive and way more reliable than finicky touch controls often found on over-ear headphones.

Her one complaint? That sometimes sudden, loud sounds — like a train rolling up to a platform — could cause audio distortion. With this new generation, Bose is providing a fix for that issue, as well as improving on all of the parts of the headphones Mangino already appreciated. Here's the breakdown:

### Design upgrades

At a casual glance, these headphones look similar to the first generation, but come with a few upgrades. For starters, the ear cups have more of an oval shape to provide a fit that's better for maximizing passive noise cancellation without sacrificing comfortable wear. The headband is more plush with improved sliders for easier adjustment, and the button placement is even more intuitive than the first generation, according to Bose.

SEE ALSO:  [The 6 most comfortable headphones are like small hugs for your ears](/roundup/most-comfortable-headphones-earbuds)

Of course, there are also the three new colorways: eucalyptus green, dewdrop mint, and rosewood mauve, featuring two-toned palettes for a more striking design.

### Sound upgrades

One of the most major differences between the OG QuietComforts and QC Ultras was the presence of spatial audio on the latter. That difference is no longer. Bose introduces TrueSpatial technology on the second generation QuietComfort headphones, featuring spatial audio listening modes in Still, Motion, and Cinema modes.

Bose also introduces lossless playback via the USB-C cable, which can still charge the headphones while they're being used.

### Noise cancellation

Bose has always been solid in the noise cancellation space, but they're making even more improvements to their tech (now called QuietControl). As the name suggests, the QC line is focused on comfort, so the headphones are intentionally left with some gaps to allow for all-day wear. According to Bose, those gaps will be addressed due to improved tech in the six-microphone system and adaptive controls in the headphones.

Spikes of noise, as Mangino mentioned, will also be addressed in Aware Mode with the addition of ActiveSense response, which engages some noise cancellation for mitigating the impact of the spikes.

The headphones are available to preorder as of Aug. 8 on Bose's website and will be widely available on Aug. 13. Her one complaint? That sometimes sudden, loud sounds — like a train rolling up to a platform — could cause audio distortion. With this new generation, Bose is providing a fix for that issue, as well as improving on all of the parts of the headphones Mangino already appreciated. Spikes of noise, as Mangino mentioned, will also be addressed in Aware Mode with the addition of ActiveSense response, which engages some noise cancellation for mitigating the impact of the spikes.
args.summary: Mashable reports on the launch of Bose QuietComfort (2nd gen) headphones, announced on Aug. 6, 2026, with preorders starting Aug. 8 and wide availability on Aug. 13. Priced at $359 (same as the first gen), the headphones feature upgraded noise cancellation (QuietControl), Bose TrueSpatial audio with Immersive Audio modes (Still, Motion, Cinema), six microphones, Bluetooth 5.4, multipoint connectivity, 24-hour battery life (18 hours with Immersive Audio), USB-C lossless audio up to 24bit/48kHz, a three-band custom equalizer, and a 15-minute quick charge for 2.5 hours of playback. Design upgrades include more oval-shaped ear cups for better passive noise cancellation, a plusher headband, improved sliders, and more intuitive button placement. New two-toned colorways include eucalyptus green, dewdrop mint, and rosewood mauve (limited editions) alongside classic black and white smoke. The article notes that the headphones fix audio distortion issues from sudden loud sounds via ActiveSense response in Aware Mode. At $359, they are positioned cheaper than the Bose QuietComfort Ultra (2nd gen) at $449.

March 16, 2026

PRESS RELEASE

Apple introduces AirPods Max 2

Powered by H2, AirPods Max are better than ever with more effective ANC, enhanced sound quality, and new features like Adaptive Audio and Live Translation

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced [AirPods Max 2](https://www.apple.com/airpods-max/), bringing even better Active Noise Cancellation (ANC), elevated sound quality, and intelligent features to the iconic over-ear design. Powered by H2, features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation, and Live Translation come to AirPods Max for the first time. The new AirPods Max also unlock creative possibilities for podcasters, musicians, and content creators, with useful features like studio-quality audio recording and camera remote.

AirPods Max 2 will be available to order starting March 25 in midnight, starlight, orange, purple, and blue, with availability beginning early next month.

“With the incredible performance of H2, AirPods Max are upgraded with up to 1.5x more effective ANC for the ultimate all-day listening experience,” said Eric Treski, Apple’s director of Audio Product Marketing. “The sound quality is remarkably clean, rich, and acoustically detailed — and when combined with capabilities like Personalized Spatial Audio, AirPods Max 2 deliver a profoundly immersive experience.”

**Active Noise Cancellation Gets Even Better**

Thanks to H2 and new computational audio algorithms, AirPods Max 2 deliver ANC that’s up to 1.5x more effective than the previous generation. This reduces even more noise — like airplane engines or commuter trains — so users can fully immerse themselves in music, work, or phone calls.

With a new digital signal processing algorithm optimized for H2 and the microphone array on AirPods Max, Transparency sounds even more natural so users can stay aware of their environment and those around them.

**Highest-Fidelity Listening Experience**

AirPods Max 2 feature a new high dynamic range amplifier for even cleaner audio while maintaining the incredible sound signature of AirPods Max. Spatial Audio content sounds better than ever, with improved localization of instruments, more accurate and consistent bass response, and more natural-sounding mids and highs.

For the highest-quality audio across music, movies, and games, the new AirPods Max support 24-bit, 48 kHz lossless audio when connected with the included USB-C cable. Lossless audio and ultra-low latency audio enable music creators to fully utilize AirPods Max throughout their entire professional workflow on Logic Pro and other music creation apps. Using the USB-C cable, AirPods Max are the only headphones that let musicians both create and mix in Personalized Spatial Audio with head tracking.1

Reduced wireless audio latency also makes gaming even better. For those using AirPods Max 2 and playing in Game Mode, iOS, macOS, and iPadOS games feel even more responsive and immersive.

**Intelligent Features Come to AirPods Max**

H2 ushers in an array of features that make AirPods Max 2 even more intelligent and convenient.

**AirPods Max 2 and the Environment**

Apple 2030 is the company’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by the end of this decade by reducing product emissions from their three biggest sources: materials, electricity, and transportation. AirPods Max 2 are made with 100 percent recycled rare earth elements in all magnets, 100 percent recycled polyester in the ear cushion, and 100 percent recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards. The paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based and can be easily recycled.6

This YouTube video from Matt Talks Tech (dated November 12, 2025) discusses leaks and rumors about the AirPods Max 2. The original AirPods Max was released in late 2020, with only minor updates in 2024 (USB-C and new colors). Key points from the video:

- **Release Date**: According to leakers Mark Gurman and Ming-Chi Kuo, the AirPods Max 2 is not a priority for Apple. Production is unlikely to start until 2027 at the earliest, meaning the first-gen model will be about 7 years old by then.
- **Price**: Expected to remain at the current price point of over $500.
- **Chip Upgrade**: The current H1 chip will likely be upgraded to at least H2, possibly H3 (which may debut in AirPods Pro 4 in 2026).
- **Design Changes**: Potential redesign to make the headphones lighter (current model is heavy), possibly using new materials like titanium (though expensive). The mesh canopy and the case (described as "awful") may also be redesigned.
- **ANC**: The H3 chip could improve active noise cancellation sample rates.
- **Context**: Apple has reportedly spent significant R&D on the AirPods Max but saw insufficient sales, deprioritizing the product line. The video speculates that features from upcoming AirPods Pro 4 may transfer to the AirPods Max 2, similar to how the first-gen AirPods Max inherited features from AirPods Pro first-gen.

[Anker Soundcore headphones](https://www.soundguys.com/tag/anker/) have continuously impressed us with their extensive features and affordable price. The latest model we’ve tested is the Anker Soundcore Space One, which promises great noise canceling and sound quality for only $100. Find out if these headphones are the new top-value offering in our Anker Soundcore Space One review.

*Editor’s note: this article was updated on November 13, 2024, to include a comparison to the Anker Soundcore Space One Pro.*

**About this Anker Soundcore Space One review:** We tested the Anker Soundcore Space One over one week. The headphones ran firmware version 01.87, and the Soundcore app and version 3.5.2. Anker provided the unit for this review.

The Anker Soundcore Space One are for anyone seeking noise canceling headphones that don’t break the bank.



## What’s it like to use Anker Soundcore Space One?

Chase Bernath / SoundGuys

Along with the headphones, you get a cloth carrying case, USB-C charging cable, and 3.5mm auxiliary cable.

Props are due for Anker Soundcore designing a cheap headphone that doesn’t look cheap. The color options include Jet Black, Sky Blue, and Latte Cream, the latter finish sported by our review model. From a distance, you could easily be tricked into thinking this is a $400 headphone from a company such as Sony, Bose, or Apple, especially in this gorgeous Latter Cream colorway.

You may be let down when you realize that the shiny, metallic-looking exterior is plastic. The plastic construction keeps the headphones lightweight, providing a comfortable wearing experience. Both the headband and ear pads are made from soft silicone. The headband clicks into various sizes, while the ear cups swivel and fold for excellent portability.

Like most over-ear style headphones, the Anker Soundcore Space One don’t have an [IP water resistance rating](https://www.soundguys.com/decoding-ip-ratings-16550/). I would not recommend taking these headphones to the gym or out in the rain.



## How do you control the Anker Soundcore Space One?

Physical buttons on both ear cups provide onboard playback controls. Inside the left ear cup is a sensor that detects whether or not you are wearing the headphones and pauses your music accordingly. You can also cover the left ear cup to activate transparency mode quickly or have the headphones set to enable transparency mode when you start speaking. All of these controls are adjustable within the Soundcore app.

| Power button | NC button | Play/pause button | Volume up button | Volume down button |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Single press | Power button | NC button Switch ambient sound modes (ANC / Transparency) | Play/pause button Play / pause, answer/end call, | Volume up button Volume up | Volume down button Volume down |
| Press and hold | Power button Power on / off | NC button | Play/pause button Reject call, mute microphone, activate voice assistant | Volume up button Next track | Volume down button Previous track |



## Should you use the Soundcore app for the Anker Soundcore Space One?

The Soundcore app provides a very comprehensive experience for the Space One headphones. You get everything you would expect from a companion app, such as battery information, firmware updates, control customization, and some nifty extras. Within the Ambient Sound section, you can switch between noise canceling and transparency mode, adjust the strength of the noise canceling, and enable wind noise reduction.

The biggest strength of the Soundcore app is found within the Sound Effects section, where you’ll find plenty of options to adjust the headphones’ sound. You can select from one of the many [equalizer](https://www.soundguys.com/how-to-eq-bluetooth-headphones-62430/) presets or build your own custom EQ setting using the eight-band equalizer. If you aren’t as audio savvy, try out the HearID Sound section, which builds a custom eq based on a hearing test and some information about you, such as your age.

A unique feature of the app is a built-in decibel meter. You’ll find it at the bottom of the app in the Safe Volume section, where you can see exactly how loud your current music is. This is great for protecting your ears from [noise-induced hearing loss](https://www.soundguys.com/noise-induced-hearing-loss-17420/), and you can limit the maximum headphone volume from within this section of the app.



## How do the Anker Soundcore Space One connect?

Chase Bernath / SoundGuys

The bottom of the ear cups feature the control buttons and charging and auxiliary cable input.

A wide variety of connectivity options are available with the Anker Soundcore Space One. Using the included auxiliary cable, you can listen wired. The headphones have Bluetooth 5.3 for wireless listening, which supports advanced Bluetooth features such as [Auracast](https://www.soundguys.com/bluetooth-auracast-108832/). [LDAC codec](https://www.soundguys.com/the-best-bluetooth-ldac-headphones-29515/) support provides high bit rate streaming with compatible Android devices, and you can use the regular [SBC and AAC codecs](https://www.soundguys.com/understanding-bluetooth-codecs-15352/) for all other devices.

Unlike the [Anker Soundcore Life Q30](https://www.soundguys.com/anker-soundcore-life-q30-review-109887/) headphones, the Space One don’t support NFC pairing. However, you still get Bluetooth [Multipoint](https://www.soundguys.com/bluetooth-multipoint-explained-28601/) to pair to two devices simultaneously.

It’s also worth noting that while the headphones charge using a USB-C port, you can’t plug into a USB source and get audio over the cable, a feature that is becoming standard in this space.

Pairing the Anker Soundcore Space One headphones to your device is a simple process:

1. Press and hold the power button on the headphones for 5 seconds to enter pairing mode.
2. Search for the Soundcore Space One headphones in the Bluetooth settings on your device.
3. Press the power button twice to pair to a second device using Bluetooth multipoint.



## How long does the Anker Soundcore Space One battery last?

Chase Bernath / SoundGuys

This wear-detection sensor automatically pauses your music when you remove the headphones, helping preserve battery life.

In [our battery test](https://www.soundguys.com/headphone-reviews-why-we-test-18172/), the Anker Soundcore Space One lasted 42 hours and 57 minutes (ANC on) on a single charge. This is in line with the promised battery life of the product, as Anker Soundcore states the headphones should last 40 hours with ANC and 55 hours without. This is pretty good battery life for wireless ANC headphones. You can charge the headphones via the USB-C input when you run out of juice.

The company states that charging the Anker Soundcore Space One for 5 minutes will yield 4 hours of playback time.



## How well do the Anker Soundcore Space One cancel noise?

The Anker Soundcore Space One headphones do a good job blocking environmental noise. [Passive isolation](https://www.soundguys.com/what-is-isolation-12506/) from the foam ear pads blocks a noticeable amount of mid and high-frequency noise, such as people talking. Enabling [active noise canceling](https://www.soundguys.com/how-noise-cancelling-headphones-work-12380/) attenuates low-frequency noise, such as the rumble of an airplane engine.

With the headphones on and ANC set to maximum, most noise around you will only sound about one-quarter as loud as without the headphones. While this isn’t as good as the [best noise canceling headphones](https://www.soundguys.com/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-5220/), it is still impressive for headphones in this price range.

Loading chart ...

You can adjust the strength of the noise canceling from within the Soundcore app. You can also enable adaptive ANC, which dynamically adjusts the strength of the noise canceling depending on how loud your environment is.

On the flip side, if you want to hear what’s happening around you, the headphones have a transparency mode. It’s one of the better transparency modes I’ve listened to, as the environmental noise sounds realistic with minimal added noise.



## How do the Anker Soundcore Space One sound?

The Space One sound similar to most Anker Soundcore headphones. These aren’t designed for critical listening but offer an exciting sound that most casual listeners will enjoy.

### Multi-Dimensional Audio Quality Scores (MDAQS)

The chart below shows how the sound of the Anker Soundcore Space One was assessed by the Multi-Dimensional Audio Quality Score ([MDAQS](https://www.soundguys.com/what-is-mdaqs-104949/)) algorithm from HEAD acoustics.

The Space One score highly in Timbre and Immersiveness.

These are impressive scores: according to our virtual panel of listeners, most people will enjoy the default sound of these headphones even before adjusting the sound in the Soundcore app.

Timbre (MOS-T) represents how faithfully the earbuds reproduce the frequency spectrum and temporal resolution (timing information).

Distortion (MOS-D) represents non-linearities and added noise: higher scores mean cleaner reproduction.

Immersiveness (MOS-I) represents perceived source width and positioning: how well virtual sound sources are defined in three-dimensional space.

See [here](https://www.soundguys.com/what-is-mdaqs-104949/) for an explanation of MDAQS, how it works, and how it was developed.

### Reviewer’s notes

*Editor’s note: this review uses a hover-enabled glossary to describe sound quality based on a consensus vocabulary. You can read about it*[***here***](https://www.soundguys.com/headphone-reviews-problems-67837/)*.*

### Objective Measurements

Loading chart ...

In the [chart](https://www.soundguys.com/how-to-read-charts-23129/) above, you can see how the [frequency response](https://www.soundguys.com/frequency-response-explained-16507/) of the Anker Soundcore Space One compares to [our headphone preference curve](https://www.soundguys.com/soundguys-house-curve-54290/). The headphones have a U-shaped frequency response that amplifies low and high frequencies while attenuating mid-frequencies. This is common for consumer headphones as they create a more “exciting” sound at the cost of detail in mid-range sounds such as vocals, piano, and guitar.

The Soundcore app has over a dozen EQ presets. We’ve tested a few of the most popular presets to show you how they impact the frequency response of the headphones.

### Bass Reducer EQ Preset

Loading chart ...

Using the bass reducer preset on the Space One creates a sound more aligned with our headphone preference curve. This should be the first preset you try if you don’t like the default sound of the headphones.

### Bass Booster EQ Preset

Loading chart ...

If you want to see just how much bass you can push out of the headphones, the bass booster preset is for you.

Loading chart ...

The yellow dotted line shows the frequency response of the Anker Soundcore Space One with ANC off. As you can see, ANC has little impact on the headphones’ sound besides the deep sub-bass frequencies.

Loading chart ...

The chart above shows the frequency response measured with a passive (unpowered) wired connection (the dotted yellow line). As you can see, there is significantly more emphasis on low-mid frequencies when listening wired with the headphones turned off. Most people are not going to like this sound, so you’ll want to make sure to keep the headphones powered up.



## Can you use the Anker Soundcore Space One for phone calls?

With three microphones and an AI algorithm to isolate vocals, the Anker Soundcore Space One performs well when taking calls on the go. In our microphone demonstrations below, voices are clear.

### Anker Soundcore Space One microphone demo (Ideal conditions):

### How does the microphone sound to you?

This is a product review of the **Anker Soundcore Space One** headphones, published on SoundGuys by Chase Bernath on November 13, 2024. The headphones are priced at approximately $100 and offer luxury features at a budget price.

**Key Specifications:**
- Battery Life: 55 hours (wireless), 42h57m with ANC on (tested)
- Charging: USB-C (5 min charge = 4 hours playback)
- Bluetooth 5.3 with LDAC, SBC, AAC codecs
- Weight: 263g
- Plastic construction, closed-back design
- Multipoint support (2 devices)
- Companion app (Soundcore) with EQ, HearID, safe volume monitor
- Physical buttons for controls, wear detection sensor
- No IP rating, no touch controls, no audio over USB

**Performance:**
- ANC effectively reduces noise to about 1/4 perceived loudness; adjustable via app
- Decent transparency mode
- U-shaped frequency response (emphasized bass and treble); EQ presets available
- MDAQS scores: Timbre 4.5, Distortion 2.3, Immersiveness 3.9, Overall 3.8
- Good microphone performance for calls across various conditions

**Comparisons:**
- vs. Space One Pro ($200): Standard Space One preferred for sound quality; Pro offers more compact folding
- vs. Space Q45 (more expensive): Minimal differences; Space One recommended for most users
- Alternatives: 1MORE SonoFlow, Anker Soundcore Life Q30

**Bottom Line:** The reviewer recommends these headphones for their strong feature set, good ANC, companion app, and battery life at a $100 price point, noting they compete well with flagship models from Sony, Bose, and Apple at a fraction of the cost.

The Soundcore by Anker Space One Over-the-Ear Headphones can block ambient noise on a flight, in a coffee shop, or during a daily commute. Adaptive Active Noise Cancellation reduces traffic, conversation, and other constant ambient sound, and Transparency Mode lets surrounding noise through when you need to stay aware. The 40mm dynamic drivers deliver detail across vocals, mids, and bass, and the Soundcore app adds customizable EQ and hi-res LDAC support. Bluetooth 5.3 supports multipoint pairing for two devices, and battery life lasts up to 40 hours with ANC on or 55 hours without it.

## Quality over-ear headphones that look and feel fantastic

The Space One headphones deliver clear vocals, balanced mids, and tight bass across most music genres. The 40mm dynamic drivers produce loud, full sound at moderate listening levels, and LDAC hi-res support adds detail over compatible Bluetooth codecs. Customizable EQ through the Soundcore app fine-tunes bass, mids, and treble for podcasts, music, or audiobooks. Bass response holds up at low volumes for late-night listening and remains distortion-free at higher volumes. Volume is loud enough for personal listening, even in high-ambient-noise environments.

The Space One’s noise cancellation suppresses constant background noise, such as in airplane cabins, office HVAC systems, and on buses. Transparency Mode pulls in surrounding sound through the earcup microphones, so you can hear announcements, conversations, or your environment without removing the headphones. Adaptive ANC automatically adjusts cancellation strength based on detected noise levels, while the Soundcore app provides manual control over ANC and transparency settings. Voice prompts announce ANC mode changes, battery status, and connection state through the headphone speakers.

The memory foam earcups are covered with a soft synthetic material that forms a seal to passively isolate and enhance the performance of the Active Noise Cancellation (ANC). Instead of focusing all its weight on one spot like many headphones do, the padding is distributed along the entire length of the headband so there are no hot spots. When folded down, the ear cups fit into the included travel case. Additionally, you can adjust the sliders to fit your head size. With an approximate weight of about 9 oz., these are lightweight enough to wear for many hours without placing too much strain on your head.

The Space One makes a few trade-offs typical of headphones in this price range. ANC works against constant background noise but doesn’t reach the depth of flagship headphones, and the build is mostly plastic. However, you still get adaptive noise cancellation, multipoint Bluetooth pairing, and up to 40 hours of battery life with ANC active. Unfortunately, microphone quality holds up in quiet environments but degrades in windy or noisy outdoor settings.

The Soundcore by Anker Space One Over-the-Ear Headphones deliver adaptive noise cancellation, hi-res LDAC support, and up to 40 hours of battery life in a budget-friendly package, and at $80, they’re a great deal for entry-level over-ear headphones. Plus, everyone deserves to feel cool and tech-forward when they wear their over-ear headphones.

But these days, consumer tech products can be all or nothing. You either cough up hundreds of dollars for the best of the best, or pay less for less functional, less aesthetically pleasing, lower-quality tech. Yet everyone has an inner Goldilocks who wants something right in the middle -- and that's hard to find.

So, what if I told you that you could have a good-quality pair of fashionable headphones with luxury features for only $80? The Soundcore Space One headphones arrived one year after the [Space Q45](https://us.soundcore.com/products/space-q45-a3040011#link={%22role%22:%22standard%22,%22href%22:%22https://us.soundcore.com/products/space-q45-a3040011%22,%22target%22:%22_blank%22,%22absolute%22:%22%22,%22linkText%22:%22Space Q45 headphones%22}), which are popular for their impressive active noise canceling (ANC) capabilities despite their $150 price tag. But the Space One headphones have better ANC, a sleeker look, and enhanced microphone performance compared to their predecessor.

**Also: [What is Bluetooth 6.0? How the latest standard is changing audio right before our eyes](https://www.zdnet.com/article/what-is-bluetooth-6-headphones/)**

For a pair of [$100 headphones](https://www.zdnet.com/article/best-cheap-headphones/), everything about the Space One headphones is impressive. These cans use adaptive noise cancellation technology to detect and eliminate noise disturbances around you. And they do a decent job at blocking clicking sounds, such as typing on a keyboard or clicking a mouse.

Droning noises, like a refrigerator, lawnmower, AC unit, or the hum of a plane, can sneak past the Space One's ANC, but turning the volume right over 50% eliminates this problem. The Space One headphones deliver full-bodied bass, mids that aren't hollow, and treble that's enjoyable and clear without piercing your eardrums. These headphones don't deliver the deepest bass, so if you don't like boomy, cranium-vibrating bass, these cans are for you.

**Also: [You're not getting the optimal sound from your headphones and speakers without this setting](https://www.zdnet.com/article/what-is-eq-and-how-it-improves-headphone-speaker-sound/)**

When I listened to "Part II (On The Run)" by Beyoncé and Jay-Z, the bassline was clear enough to keep me in the groove, but it lacked the deep punch that makes a song feel like it's in my bones. Still, the mids remain clear and natural, while the treble is steady enough to bring out small details in the song without sounding shrill.

![Soundcore Space One headphones in Sky Blue hanging from a brick corner]()

Jada Jones/ZDNET

The Space One headphones are the latest in Soundcore's Space lineup, and their name fits their design: they have a sleek, outer-space vibe. Soundcore has blended matte finishes with chrome details, and the Sky Blue color I tried solidifies the galactic feel.

**Also: [Are these $50 headphones on Amazon legit? I tested them and couldn't believe what I heard](https://www.zdnet.com/article/haylou-s40-headphones-review/)**

The Space One ear cups are made from polyurethane leather and are more circular than oval, providing a mix of over- and on-ear fit, leaning more toward on-ear.

Instead of sporting an elongated oval ear cup shape like the [Bose QuietComfort 45 headphones](https://www.zdnet.com/article/these-are-my-go-to-headphones-for-all-day-listening-and-theyre-not-airpods/), the circular Space One earcups can press the ears a little too tight. I wore the Space One headphones for two-hour increments, then removed them briefly to alleviate ear fatigue.

But you'll need plenty of breaks before the battery gives out, as you can get 55 hours of playtime with these headphones with ANC off. With ANC on, the Space One headphones will last 40 hours, and just 5 minutes of charging can give you 4 hours of playtime.

**Also: [These Sennheiser headphones are a world's first for audio connectivity - and I'm excited](https://www.zdnet.com/home-and-office/home-entertainment/sennheiser-rs-275-tv-headphones-auracast-connectivity/)**

Now, let's get into the extra features Space One gives you that some headphones, at double, triple, or quadruple their price, won't. First, the Soundcore companion app is a highly comprehensive hub for your EQ preferences. In the app, you can create a Custom HearID, which asks you a few prompts before creating a bespoke EQ setting based on your responses.

Additionally, the Soundcore app offers 22 EQ presets that adjust the Space One EQ settings to deliver the best sound for the music you're listening to. For example, the Pop EQ setting will amplify the treble and mids while slightly decreasing the bass, and the Hip-Hop setting will boost the bass, lower the treble, and slightly raise the mids. These extremely tailored EQ settings don't come with the [Bose 700 headphones](https://www.zdnet.com/article/best-bluetooth-headphones/), which cost $380.

The Space One headphones are equipped with Wearing Detection, a feature that pauses music when they sense you've taken them off your head and resumes playback when you put them back on. This is a feature you won't have with the [Beats Studio Pro](https://www.zdnet.com/article/the-beats-studio-pro-are-so-close-to-being-my-dream-headphones/), which retail for $350.

**Also: [I replaced my AirPods Pro with Sony XM6 earbuds for a month - and I'm nearly sold](https://www.zdnet.com/article/sony-wf-1000-xm6-review/)**

Easy Chat can be enabled in the Soundcore app and will lower the volume of your music when the Space One headphones detect your voice, assuming you're trying to have a conversation. Then, the Space One headphones will amplify the other person's voice, allowing you to hear them better, all without removing your cans. You won't find this feature in the [AirPods Max](https://www.zdnet.com/product/apple-airpods-max/), despite their $550 asking price.

There's only one real complaint I have about these headphones: the carrying case -- or carrying dust bag, I should say. This is a bit tedious and isn't a direct critique of the headphones, but having a convenient carrying case adds to the experience -- and it's something the Space One lacks.

Inutile carrying cases that make your precious headphones susceptible to damage, like the AirPods Max case, don't give you a safe place to store your device. Hardshell cases (my preference) tend to come with more expensive headphones, but a soft, zip-up case would still do the Space One more justice than the drawstring bag they come with.

## ZDNET's buying advice

All in all, the [Space One headphones](https://cc.zdnet.com/v1/otc/00hQi47eqnEWQ6T9d4QLBUc?merchant=05kie42h3YvHwjr4G1w80Qq&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2Fdp%2FB0C6KKQ7ND&app_deeplink=1) are great for their low price. I would recommend these headphones for people who don't want the fanciest, most expensive headphones, but don't want to sell themselves short with cheaply made ones either.

The Soundcore Space One headphones won't impress audiophiles, but they will give the average listener everything they're looking for in a good-quality pair of headphones. If you want to make $80 stretch as far as it can for a pair of headphones, hop on the Space One.

TL;DR

* The Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless launches June 16, 2026 at $399.99 in Black, White, and Denim colorways
* Upgraded ANC system with eight microphones (four per side) promises up to 3x better voice noise reduction
* aptX Lossless Bluetooth codec support delivers CD-quality wireless audio, a feature the Sony WH-1000XM6 lacks
* A user-replaceable 700 mAh battery rated for 57 hours of ANC playback sets a new repairability standard
* Ships with Bluetooth 5.4, with Bluetooth 6.0 and LE Audio arriving via firmware update

Nearly four years after the Momentum 4 Wireless cemented Sennheiser’s reputation as a serious contender in the premium headphone space, the German audio brand has officially unveiled its successor. The Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless arrives on June 16 at $399.99 USD, and it’s packed with upgrades that directly target every weakness reviewers and users flagged in the previous generation.

The timing is deliberate. Sony released its WH-1000XM6 last year to strong reviews, and Bose followed with the QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) shortly after. Sennheiser has been conspicuously absent from the flagship refresh cycle until now, and the Momentum 5 reads like a calculated response to both.

The launch also arrives as audio brands are adding more software and [AI-driven features to earbuds and headphones.](https://memeburn.com/ankers-soundcore-liberty-5-pro-new-earbuds-bring-ai-to-your-ears/) 

## **What’s New in the Sennheiser Momentum 5**

The Momentum 5 keeps the same 42mm dynamic transducer that powered its predecessor, a driver originally inspired by Sennheiser’s legendary HD 600-series open-back headphones. But nearly everything around that driver has been upgraded.

The biggest addition is **aptX Lossless codec support through Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Sound platform**. This means the Momentum 5 can deliver CD-quality audio over Bluetooth when paired with a compatible source device. The full codec roster includes SBC, AAC, aptX, aptX HD, aptX Adaptive, and aptX Lossless. For context, the Sony WH-1000XM6 relies on LDAC as its highest-quality wireless option, while the Bose QC Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) only added USB lossless audio with their latest revision.

The headphones also carry **Hi-Res Audio certification from the Japan Audio Society**, confirming a frequency response extending up to 40 kHz and support for 24-bit/96 kHz audio. When connected via Bluetooth or USB, the range stretches from 6 Hz to 40 kHz.

On the software side, the updated Smart Control Plus companion app introduces an **eight-band equalizer**, bespoke audio presets, and an intelligent Sound Personalization engine that tailors the listening profile to your ears. A day-one firmware update adds Dolby Atmos with head-tracking for compatible [spatial audio content](https://memeburn.com/ios-27-completely-changes-operation-for-airpods-users/).

## **ANC Gets a Major Overhaul**

Active noise cancellation was the single most-requested improvement from Momentum 4 owners. [According to SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-131570/), 51% of polled readers named improved ANC as their top priority for the next Momentum.

Sennheiser responded by **doubling the microphone count dedicated to noise cancellation**, going from two per side on the Momentum 4 to four per side on the Momentum 5. The company claims this delivers **up to three times more effective reduction of ambient voice chatter** compared to the previous model. That’s a specific and measurable claim, and early reviews suggest it holds up in practice.

The additional microphones also benefit transparency mode and call quality. Sennheiser says the upgraded array produces more natural voice reproduction during phone calls, with improved handling of wind and environmental noise.

For anyone who loved the Momentum 4’s sound but felt the ANC fell short of Sony and Bose, this is the upgrade that matters most.

## **The Replaceable Battery: A Quiet Revolution**

Perhaps the most forward-thinking feature of the Momentum 5 is its **user-replaceable 700 mAh battery**. Swapping it requires nothing more than a Phillips-head screwdriver. In a category where almost every competitor glues its battery shut, this is a significant statement about product longevity.

The battery delivers **up to 57 hours of playback with ANC enabled**. That’s a slight drop from the Momentum 4’s 60-hour rating, but it still dwarfs the competition:

* **Sony WH-1000XM6:** ~30 hours with ANC
* **Bose QC Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen):** ~24 hours with ANC
* **Apple AirPods Max 2:** ~20 hours with ANC

A five-minute quick charge provides roughly three hours of listening time. And because the battery is replaceable, the Momentum 5 becomes a headphone you can realistically use for a decade rather than treating it as something you’ll replace when the battery degrades in two or three years.

This also aligns with growing regulatory pressure around device repairability. The EU’s battery regulation, which takes effect in phases, will eventually require removable batteries in many consumer electronics. Sennheiser is getting ahead of that curve.

## **Bluetooth 6.0 Ready: Future-Proofing Built In**

The Momentum 5 ships with Bluetooth 5.4, but the hardware is engineered to support **Bluetooth 6.0 through a future firmware update**. That update will also bring LE Audio support, which promises reduced latency, improved battery efficiency, and potentially better audio quality.

No timeline has been confirmed for the Bluetooth 6.0 update, but [What Hi-Fi reports](https://www.whathifi.com/headphones/sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless) that Sennheiser expects it to arrive later this year. This approach of shipping hardware that can be upgraded via software reflects a broader shift in the premium headphone market toward longer product lifecycles.

The Momentum 5 also supports Multipoint Bluetooth, allowing it to connect to two devices simultaneously.

## **Sennheiser Momentum 5 vs Sony WH-1000XM6 vs Bose QC Ultra 2: How They Compare**

Here’s a detailed breakdown of how the three flagship wireless headphones of 2025-2026 stack up against each other:

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Feature** | **Momentum 5** | **Sony WH-1000XM6** | **Bose QC Ultra 2** |
| **Price** | $399.99 | $449.99 | $449.99 |
| **Battery (ANC on)** | 57 hours | ~30 hours | ~24 hours |
| **ANC mics** | 8 (4 per side) | 12 | Not disclosed |
| **Best wireless codec** | aptX Lossless | LDAC | aptX Adaptive |
| **Replaceable battery** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Bluetooth** | 5.4 (6.0 ready) | 5.3 | 5.3 |
| **Spatial audio** | Dolby Atmos w/ head-tracking | 360 Reality Audio | Bose Immersive Audio |
| **Hi-Res certified** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (USB) |
| **Foldable** | ❌ Lay-flat only | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| **Weight** | ~290g | ~250g | ~250g |
| **USB lossless** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |

**The short version:** The Momentum 5 wins on battery life, wireless codec quality, and value. The Sony XM6 wins on ANC depth and weight. The Bose QC Ultra 2 wins on immersive audio modes and USB audio quality. None of these is a clear overall winner, which is actually great news for buyers because each excels in a different area.

## **Design and Build: Refined, Not Reinvented**

Sennheiser has played it safe with the industrial design. The Momentum 5 retains the oval ear cup shape and lay-flat form factor of its predecessor, with updated metal accents and fabric details that give it a cleaner look. The carry case is 20% smaller than the Momentum 4’s, and a new indentation on the back serves as a grip handle.

The headphones come in three colors at launch:

* **Black** (standard)
* **White** (standard)
* **Denim** (Best Buy exclusive in the US)

The packaging is plastic-free, which is a nice touch.

One area of criticism that carries over from the Momentum 4: **the headphones don’t fold**. They only lay flat, which makes them less portable than the Sony XM6 (which brought folding back after dropping it on the XM5). If you travel frequently and need compact storage, this is worth considering.

## **Sennheiser Momentum 5 Price and Availability**

The Momentum 5 Wireless goes on sale **June 16, 2026** at the following prices:

* **United States:** $399.99 USD
* **Canada:** $569.95 CAD
* **United Kingdom:** £329.90 GBP
* **Europe:** €399.90 EUR
* **Australia:** $749 AUD

Available through Sennheiser’s website, authorized retailers, Amazon, and Best Buy.

## **Should You Buy the Sennheiser Momentum 5?**

The answer depends on what you prioritize.

**Buy the Momentum 5 if:**

* Sound quality is your top priority and you want aptX Lossless
* You value battery life (57 hours is nearly double the competition)
* You want a headphone designed for longevity, with a replaceable battery
* You prefer spending $399 over $450

**Consider the Sony WH-1000XM6 instead if:**

* Maximum ANC performance matters more than anything else
* You want a foldable design for travel
* You’re already invested in Sony’s ecosystem (360 Reality Audio, Sound Connect app)

**Consider the Bose QC Ultra 2 instead if:**

* Spatial audio and immersive listening modes are important to you
* You need USB-C lossless audio for desktop use
* You prioritize ANC and don’t need long battery life

For anyone upgrading from the Momentum 4, the combination of significantly better ANC, aptX Lossless support, and the replaceable battery makes a compelling case. The $50 price increase from the M4’s original $349 is offset by the feature gains.

## **FAQs**

### **When does the Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless come out?**

The Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless launches on June 16, 2026. It will be available through Sennheiser’s website, Amazon, Best Buy, and authorized retailers worldwide.

### **How much does the Sennheiser Momentum 5 cost?**

The Momentum 5 is priced at $399.99 in the United States, £329.90 in the UK, €399.90 in Europe, $569.95 in Canada, and $749 in Australia.

### **Is the Sennheiser Momentum 5 better than the Sony WH-1000XM6?**

It depends on your priorities. The Momentum 5 offers superior battery life (57 hours vs ~30 hours), aptX Lossless codec support, and a replaceable battery at a lower price ($399 vs $449). The Sony WH-1000XM6 has a stronger ANC system with 12 microphones and a foldable design. For listeners who prioritize audio quality above all else, the Momentum 5 has the edge; for ANC-first buyers, the Sony remains the benchmark.

### **Does the Sennheiser Momentum 5 support Bluetooth 6.0?**

The Momentum 5 ships with Bluetooth 5.4, but its hardware is designed to support Bluetooth 6.0 through a future firmware update. Sennheiser has not confirmed a specific timeline for this update, but reports indicate it could arrive later in 2026.

### **Can you replace the battery on the Sennheiser Momentum 5?**

Yes. The Momentum 5 features a user-replaceable 700 mAh battery that can be swapped using a standard Phillips-head screwdriver. This is one of its standout features, as nearly every competing headphone has a non-removable battery.

### **Is the Sennheiser Momentum 5 worth upgrading from the Momentum 4?**

If ANC performance was your main complaint with the Momentum 4, the answer is yes. The doubled microphone array and aptX Lossless support represent meaningful improvements. The replaceable battery also adds long-term value. However, if you’re satisfied with your Momentum 4’s sound and ANC, the upgrade is nice-to-have rather than essential.

args.summary: The Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless headphones were officially unveiled, launching June 16, 2026, at $399.99 USD ($50 less than the Sony WH-1000XM6). Key upgrades include: aptX Lossless Bluetooth codec for CD-quality wireless audio; an overhauled ANC system with eight microphones (four per side) delivering up to 3x better voice noise reduction; a user-replaceable 700 mAh battery rated for 57 hours of ANC playback (dwarfing Sony's ~30 hours and Bose's ~24 hours); Bluetooth 5.4 with future Bluetooth 6.0 and LE Audio support via firmware update; and Dolby Atmos with head-tracking via a day-one firmware update. # **Introducing MOMENTUM 5 Wireless: Your Sound Revelation Starts Here**

[Headphones & Soundbars](/category/headphones--soundbars)

May 25, 2026

## **The Sennheiser brand’s newest portable powerhouse is an escape into high-fidelity sound, enriched with spatial audio and a suite of sophisticated capabilities.**

***Hanover, Germany – May 26, 2026***– **The Sennheiser brand today announces** ***MOMENTUM 5 Wireless*****, the most capable and user-focused evolution of the acclaimed headphone series yet.** The newest *MOMENTUM* preserves the category-defining sound and battery performance of the platinum-selling line while introducing meaningful enhancements to elevate everyday listening for the modern audio enthusiast. ​  
​​  
​​  
​

> *"With MOMENTUM 5 Wireless, we focused on refining the entire experience without straying from the formula that made its predecessor such a success,"* said Product Manager Sreenath ‘Sri’ Unnikrishnan, *"These enhancements enrich the overall functionality while still capturing the magic you feel every time you press play.”*

[![](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/2c620991-a11b-4daf-9796-e58e01fb91f9/-/format/auto/Untitled)](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/2c620991-a11b-4daf-9796-e58e01fb91f9/Untitled)

*MOMENTUM 5 Wireless features spatial audio with head-tracking and a user-replaceable battery*

**Signature Performance** ​  
​*MOMENTUM 5 Wireless* carries forward the acclaimed 42mm transducer from its predecessor, which is meticulously manufactured at the brand’s state-of-the-art facility in Tullamore, Ireland. It is inspired by the famed HD 600-series headphones and tuned for full-bodied sound with dynamic bass. This latest generation *MOMENTUM* advances its sonic possibilities even further with Hi-Res Audio certification, and Snapdragon Sound™ technology featuring BluetoothⓇ audio codec support up to aptX™ Lossless. Using the free Smart Control Plus companion app’s new 8-band EQ, bespoke presets, and intelligent Sound Personalization engine, the iconic house sound can be shaped to practically any preference with ease. ​

**Total Immersion** ​  
​The newest *MOMENTUM’s* rich and exciting sound is further magnified by what the listener *won’t hear*, as it is up to three times more effective at reducing distracting voice chatter with its supercharged active noise cancelling system. The number of microphones dedicated to ANC and transparency duties has doubled, with four microphones per side yielding across-the-board improvements at reducing droning airplane cabin noise and more natural voice quality on calls.

[![](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/f652a9fd-2e73-4532-9c9d-40ab31200953/-/format/auto/Untitled)](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/f652a9fd-2e73-4532-9c9d-40ab31200953/Untitled)

*MOMENTUM 5 Wireless boasts up to 3x more effective ANC against ambient voices* ​

Designed to improve over time, the *MOMENTUM 5 Wireless* platform gives owners new and optimized capabilities through firmware updates to the DSP and wireless engines. For example, early adopters will be greeted with day one updates, unlocking Dolby AtmosⓇ with head-tracking for next-level immersion when listening to supported Atmos encoded content1. ​ Furthermore, the hardware ships with Bluetooth 5.4 out of the box and is engineered for the future—the headphones are ready for Bluetooth 6.0 via a future firmware release. The combination of immersive audio, improved ANC and jaw-dropping sound delivers a sound revelation for brand newcomers and seasoned listeners alike. ​

> *“With MOMENTUM 5 Wireless, we’re proving that high-performance sound and environmental responsibility can — and must — exist in the same product. ​ With our new user-swappable battery, adaptable hardware, and shift to compact, plastic-free packaging, our customers will feel proud to choose a headphone meant to last.”* added Lilika Beck, President, Sennheiser Consumer Audio.

**Refreshingly Responsible** ​  
​*MOMENTUM 5 Wireless* remains an endurance champion with quick charging and up to 57 hours of battery life per charge with ANC engaged. This generation also introduces a user-replaceable 700 mAh battery, engineered to meet strenuous standards for daily use with zero impact on acoustic performance. Using only a small Phillips-head screwdriver, owners can refresh the power cell in minutes, ensuring the headphones stay in their daily rotation for years to come. This commitment to efficiency also extends to the storage case—now 20% smaller—and smaller, plastic-free packaging designed to minimize the total environmental footprint during transit. Also included in the case are a USB Type-C charging cable and 3.5mm analog audio cable for connection to in-flight entertainment systems, laptops, and more.

[![](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/5bc7a9f0-7324-489a-a67c-15b2148f432f/-/format/auto/Untitled)](https://cdn.uc.assets.prezly.com/5bc7a9f0-7324-489a-a67c-15b2148f432f/Untitled)

*MOMENTUM 5 Wireless in black, denim, and white colorways* ​

**Availability**

*MOMENTUM 5 Wireless* will be available in Black, White, and Denim colorways, with a suggested retail price of $399.99 USD. Audio enthusiasts in the USA can get their sound revelation starting June 16th at sennheiser-hearing.com and select retailers.

---

*1* *Immersive audio and head-tracking require a firmware update via the Smart Control Plus app. Playback requires an Atmos-enabled source device and content from supported spatial audio platforms.*

# Sennheiser MOMENTUM 5 Wireless Review: Did Sennheiser Just Undercut the HDB 630?

Does Sennheiser MOMENTUM 5 Wireless deliver enough with Dolby Atmos, aptX Lossless, stronger ANC, and a replaceable battery at $399?

![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/534f2170f4f7792533a390ae930afece?s=40&d=mm&r=g)

[Ian White](https://www.ecoustics.com/author/ian-white/ "Posts by Ian White")

* [+ Whatsapp](whatsapp://send?text=Sennheiser MOMENTUM 5 Wireless Review: Did Sennheiser Just Undercut the HDB 630? https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/sennheiser-momentum-5/)

![2026 Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless Headphones in Black with Travel Case](https://www.ecoustics.com/wp-content/uploads/sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-with-case.jpg "Sennheiser Momentum 5")

The **Sennheiser MOMENTUM 5 Wireless** arrives at a critical moment for every premium noise-cancelling headphone brand that likes sleeping at night. Sony has the new [1000X The ColleXion](https://www.ecoustics.com/products/sony-1000x-collexion-wireless-headphones/), Apple has finally pushed forward with [AirPods Max 2](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/airpods-max-2/), Bose is still leaning hard into noise cancellation with its latest QuietComfort Ultra Headphones, and [Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/bowers-wilkins-px7-s3-wireless-anc-headphones/) continues to court listeners who demand that their wireless headphones sound like high-end transducers.

That matters because Sennheiser has spent the past few years defending two different corners of the headphone market: the mainstream wireless category with the [MOMENTUM 4 Wireless](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/sennheiser-momentum-4/), and the more serious audiophile lane with the HDB 630, which we also [reviewed](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/sennheiser-hdb-630/) as a higher-performance Bluetooth headphone for listeners who prioritise sound quality over ANC performance or call quality.

## MOMENTUM 5 Wireless Keeps the MOMENTUM 4 Formula But Adds More Control

![sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-front](https://www.ecoustics.com/wp-content/uploads/sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-front.jpg)

MOMENTUM 5 (front)

The Sennheiser MOMENTUM 5 Wireless builds on the MOMENTUM 4 platform rather than replacing the basic formula. The new model keeps the 42mm transducer from its predecessor, manufactured at Sennheiser’s Tullamore, Ireland facility, and uses tuning inspired by the company’s HD 600-series headphones. Sennheiser describes the sound as full-bodied with dynamic bass, which suggests continuity with the MOMENTUM line rather than a major sonic reset.

The more practical headline may be the **user-replaceable 700 mAh battery**, which gives the $399.99 MOMENTUM 5 Wireless a real longevity advantage over rivals that still treat batteries like a countdown timer to your next purchase. Sennheiser is giving owners a way to keep the headphones they already paid for instead of nudging them toward the next model the moment battery life starts to fade.

The codec and wireless story has also been updated. MOMENTUM 5 Wireless includes Hi-Res Audio certification, Snapdragon Sound, and Bluetooth codec support up to aptX Lossless. It ships with Bluetooth 5.4, but Sennheiser says the hardware is designed to support Bluetooth 6.0 through a future firmware update.

Noise cancellation has been revised with more microphones. Sennheiser says the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless uses four microphones per side for ANC and transparency functions, doubling the microphone count used for those duties. The company claims the new system is up to three times more effective at reducing distracting voice chatter, with improvements to airplane cabin noise reduction and voice quality on calls.

## Spatial Audio Arrives, But the Replaceable Battery May Matter More

Spatial audio is included, but there are a few conditions. **Dolby Atmos with head tracking** will be enabled through a day-one firmware update in Sennheiser’s **Smart Control Plus** app, and it requires an Atmos-enabled source device plus supported Atmos content.

That should include popular devices such as recent iPhones, iPads, Macs, Apple TV 4K, many current Android phones, Fire TV devices, and other streamers or computers that support Dolby Atmos playback through services like Apple Music, Amazon Music Unlimited, TIDAL, Netflix, Disney+, or Max. The MOMENTUM 5 Wireless can handle the feature, but the phone, app, subscription tier, and content still have to line up. Naturally, audio remains a team sport whether we like it or not.

Support for Dolby Atmos-encoded content streamed through TIDAL worked properly out of the box, but head tracking was not yet enabled during my review period.

Battery life remains a major part of the story. Sennheiser rates the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless at up to 57 hours per charge with ANC engaged. The bigger practical change is the user-replaceable 700 mAh battery, which can be swapped with a small Phillips-head screwdriver.

That 60-hour battery claim looks great on paper, but real-world use landed a bit lower for me. Across several weeks of mixed listening, I averaged closer to 53 to 54 hours, depending on volume, source device, codec support, and whether I was streaming music from TIDAL and Qobuz or watching movies and TV on an iPad Pro.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

Battery drain varied by device. My iPhone 14, iPhone 17, and iPhone X burned through the charge a bit faster, while a borrowed Samsung phone came closer to the upper end of Sennheiser’s rating. Streaming hi-res content from Qobuz and TIDAL pulled those numbers down slightly, which is exactly what you would expect when asking the headphones to do more than sip compressed audio through a straw.

With ANC engaged, especially in Adaptive or Custom modes, I would set realistic expectations closer to 51 to 52 hours. That is still excellent. I used the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless on NJ Transit, inside the walking migraine known as American Dream on Memorial Day Sunday with roughly 150,000 people trying to turn a mall into a survival documentary, and during a United Airlines trip home from Las Vegas that was delayed, rerouted through George Bush Airport in Houston, then Dulles in Northern Virginia, before finally reaching Newark about 17 hours later.

After seeing **[The Wizard of Oz at Sphere](https://www.ecoustics.com/articles/wizard-oz-sphere-las-vegas/)** in Las Vegas, I thought Dorothy had the rough travel day. Turns out all she needed was a pair of ruby slippers and a unionized gate agent.

The practical takeaway is simple: the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless has more than enough stamina for a full week of commuting, travel, office use, and the kind of airport punishment that makes you question every life choice since booking basic economy. For anyone who treats wireless headphones like a daily workhorse rather than a delicate audio object, the battery life is one of the stronger reasons to consider them.

## Build Quality, Comfort, and a Travel Case That Actually Saves Space

The **MOMENTUM 5 Wireless** fold flat for travel, which helps, although they do not feel quite as premium in the hand as the **Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3** or **Px8 S2**. Those remain part of my daily rotation along with the **[HDB 630](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/sennheiser-hdb-630/)**, and Bowers still has the edge when it comes to materials and that more polished luxury feel. The Sennheiser build is still quite solid, just more practical than posh.

The headband uses braided cloth on the top side with padding underneath, and on my head, the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless feel very similar to the HDB 630. The difference is that the HDB 630 uses the same leatherette material on both the inside and outside of the headband, which gives it a slightly different tactile feel. Both are lightweight and easy to wear, and neither feels like it was designed by someone who thinks discomfort builds character.

The ear pads have the same basic issue I noticed with the HDB 630. They are soft and comfortable, but I would prefer them to be slightly firmer. They also get warm after about 30 minutes, especially during commuting or longer listening sessions. Not unbearable, not deal-breaking, but noticeable.

Clamping force is generally similar to the HDB 630 and less firm than the Bowers & Wilkins models. That matters because I have a huge head, move through trains with some force, and still somehow try to maintain the stealth profile of a ninja who has had enough of NJ Transit. The MOMENTUM 5 Wireless stayed secure without feeling tight, which is the balance you want from travel headphones that are going to see actual use rather than live in a review drawer.

Sennheiser has also reduced the overall travel footprint. The MOMENTUM 5 Wireless carrying case is 20% smaller, and the packaging is now smaller and plastic-free. Inside the case, Sennheiser includes a USB Type-C charging cable and a 3.5mm analog audio cable, so wired listening is still available for laptops, in-flight entertainment systems, and the other legacy sources that refuse to die quietly. ![sennheiser-momentum-5-case-comparison](https://www.ecoustics.com/wp-content/uploads/sennheiser-momentum-5-case-comparison.jpg)

Case Comparison: Sennheiser HDB 630 (left) vs. MOMENTUM 5 (right)

Compared to the case supplied with the more expensive **[HDB 630](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/sennheiser-hdb-630/)**, the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless case is noticeably smaller, which matters when the headphones are going into a backpack, carry-on, or that personal item you are already pretending is not overstuffed. Both models fold, so neither is a travel disaster, but the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless is clearly the more compact option.

The accessory package is where the pricing difference starts to make more sense. The HDB 630 includes extras such as the airplane adapter and Sennheiser’s BTD 700 USB Adapter; the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless does not. That makes the HDB 630 the better-equipped package for listeners who want more connection options in the box, while the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless keeps things simpler, smaller, and more mainstream. ![sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-inside-case](https://www.ecoustics.com/wp-content/uploads/sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-inside-case.jpg)

MOMENTUM 5

## Smarter App, Stronger ANC

The companion app also gets more control. The new Smart Control Plus app includes an 8-band EQ, user presets, and Sennheiser’s Sound Personalization system. That should give listeners more flexibility than a few canned tuning modes, especially for those who liked the [MOMENTUM 4](https://www.ecoustics.com/reviews/sennheiser-momentum-4/) but wanted more precise adjustment.

Advertisement. Scroll to continue reading.

One of the stronger parts of the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless experience is Sennheiser’s Smart Control Plus app. This was already one of the highlights with the HDB 630, and that carries over here. The app is comprehensive without feeling like homework, and it worked flawlessly with both Sennheiser models during my testing.

The level of control is the real win. You are not stuck with a crude choice between full ANC and transparency mode. The MOMENTUM 5 lets you adjust the level of noise cancellation, enable or disable **Anti-Wind** in ANC mode, manage **multipoint connectivity**, and turn the app’s individual tiles on or off depending on what you actually use. That last part sounds minor until you have used enough headphone apps that feel like they were organized by committee after a three-hour liquid lunch.

ANC performance is also very strong. The MOMENTUM 5 Wireless did an effective job reducing commuter noise, chatter, and the general low-level misery that comes with trains, airports, and crowded public spaces. More importantly, it does not wreck the sound. There is still a slight reduction in openness and detail with ANC engaged, and the presentation tightens up a little, but the damage is minimal.

I still prefer listening with ANC off when the environment allows it, because the MOMENTUM 5 sounds more open and natural that way. But Sennheiser has made the ANC useful without turning the music into a padded cell.

![sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-side](https://www.ecoustics.com/wp-content/uploads/sennheiser-momentum-5-wireless-headphones-black-side.jpg)

MOMENTUM 5 (side)

## Buttons, Touch Sensors, and Real-World Use

The **MOMENTUM 5 Wireless** and **HDB 630** are very similar when it comes to controls, and that is mostly a good thing. Sennheiser keeps the basics straightforward with a power button that also handles pairing, plus the expected **USB-C** connection and **3.5mm analog input** for wired listening. Nothing exotic there, and nobody needs a treasure map to find the ports.

The touch controls are where things get more personal. Sennheiser’s system works, and I will give them full credit for that. Playback, volume, track skipping, calls, ANC, and transparency mode can all be handled from the ear cup, and the gestures responded reliably during my testing. **Transparency mode can be activated with a double tap**, which is useful when someone suddenly decides your headphones are an invitation to start talking.

That said, I am still more of an app person. The controls are not bad, but after rotating through multiple headphones and wireless earbuds, each with its own secret handshake of taps, swipes, pinches, holds, and “wait, was that two fingers or three?” routines, it becomes a lot to remember. At some point, you are not controlling headphones; you are auditioning for community theater mime work.

Sennheiser’s **Smart Control Plus** app makes more sense for how I actually use headphones. It is clean, comprehensive, and easier than trying to remember every gesture sequence while standing on a train platform or walking through a crowded terminal. The touch controls are there, they work, and plenty of users will like them. I just prefer opening the app and making the adjustment without playing finger Twister on the side of my head.

As for phone calls, the MOMENTUM 5 can handle them, but I remain fundamentally opposed to taking calls through earbuds or headphones unless absolutely necessary. That is not a Sennheiser problem. That is a “please stop making me listen to people conduct business next to the avocados” problem.

## BTD 700 Dongle: Great Idea, Rough Landing With MOMENTUM 5

The **MOMENTUM 5 Wireless** has a stronger codec story than the HDB 630 in one key respect: it supports **aptX Lossless** in addition to the usual Bluetooth basics, but there is still **no LDAC** support. For Android users with the right hardware, that may not be a big issue. For Apple users, it gets more complicated because the iPhone and MacBook still do not support aptX natively. Naturally.

![Sennheiser BTD 700 USB dongle in laptop](https://www.ecoustics.com/wp-content/uploads/sennheiser-btd-700-laptop.jpg)

Sennheiser BTD 700 USB-C dongle

That is where [Sennheiser’s BTD 700 USB-C dongle](https://www.ecoustics.com/products/sennheiser-btd-700/) is supposed to help. It acts as an external Bluetooth transmitter, bypassing the device’s built-in Bluetooth stack and handling higher-quality codec support itself. In theory, that makes it a very useful add-on for getting better wireless performance from laptops, tablets, and phones that otherwise leave you stuck with more limited Bluetooth options.

The problem is that my experience with the BTD 700 and the MOMENTUM 5 Wireless was not clean. Using it with both my iPhone and MacBook, I heard audible distortion, which is not exactly the kind of “high-resolution” experience anyone is looking for. Sennheiser has confirmed that it is working on a fix, so this may be resolved through a firmware update, but as of my testing, the issue was real.
